body.notes: Re-derived and reran. Formal: for ADAM's ARIMA part F = -a 1', g = ma - a, w = 1 (a = ari coefficients per state lag), so phi = det(I + 1' L a) = ari polynomial and D = F - g w' = -ma 1', theta = ma polynomial; checked numerically on 57 and 238 matrices built by adam() itself (AC3.RN3, AC3.RN11: max abs gap of det(I-FL) and det(I-DL) to ari and ma polynomials 1.4e-14). Cross terms: ETS(A,N,N) alpha=1.9 + MA(1) theta=0.1 has whole theta = 1 + B - 0.1 B^2 (exact fractions), the product of the parts' thetas is 1 + B + 0.09 B^2, smallest root modulus 0.916 against 1.111 (AC3.RN3), so the parts-apart check accepts a model that does not forget its states (package modulus 1.0916 whole, 0.9 ETS part alone). Reproduction with new seeds, script unchanged: seed 11 n=200 (AC3.RN1): split check differs from PBH on 65/200 ETS+ARIMA and 71/200 ETS+SARIMA; seed 12 n=200 (AC3.RN2): 67/200 and 58/200; author's RN49 166/500 and 159/500; all far above the 5% rule (25/500). Both directions occur (AC3.RN1: split accepts and PBH rejects 42 and 64; reverse 23 and 7). Review of ets_arima.py: the split baseline matches the old admissible branch of adam_bounds_checker (git 094b76f4~1: smoothEigens on ETS/constant/regressors apart, AR and MA reflections for the ARIMA); generators, AR via reflection coefficients, over-differencing, structure check against adam() (30 models, max gap 4.9e-15, AC3.RN1) are correct. Caveats, not disputes: (1) the percentage depends on the generator (alpha up to 1.9, MA reflection up to 1.5, 15% over-differenced by design), so '>5%' says the parts-apart check is wrong on a non-negligible share of such models, not on real fits; (2) over-differenced MA unit roots that cancel with a difference make the split check reject models PBH accepts, a mechanism other than the ETS-ARIMA cross terms (the cross-term direction alone is 104/500 and 128/500 in RN49 and still above 25); (3) RN49 and RN50 are the same command with the same results.json hash, so they are one data set tested under two plans; (4) the 'code changed after plan' flag is benign: git diff 397f255f..acb23120 touches only lab files.

Reran with new seeds (script unchanged). Whole-model check (cancelled MA polynomial of the ARIMA form, AR stationary) against the PBH reference: seed 11 n=200 (AC3.RN1) 0 differing decisions in 200 ETS+ARIMA and 200 ETS+SARIMA models, max abs difference of the largest modulus 2.9e-13 and 1.5e-12; seed 12 n=200 (AC3.RN2) 0 and 0, max differences 7.9e-13 and 5.7e-9; author's RN50: 0, 0, 4.3e-13, 1.6e-11. Threshold 1e-6 met each time. Stronger test with an independent oracle (AC3.RN4-RN10, 1750 models, 7 seeds): a wider generator (constant state, ETS with two seasonal lags, AR up to 3, I up to 2, MA up to 3 including factors on the unit circle 1+-B, 1+B+B^2, 1+B^2, 1-B+B^2, rational parameters, exact Fraction determinants and exact gcd(theta, phi) instead of cyclotomic-only cancellation): the cyclotomic-cancelled check (the author's functions) disagrees with the exact gcd oracle on 0 of 1750 models, so cancelling only Phi_n is enough here; the ones that cancel (admissible MA unit root) were 3 to 8 per 250. Limitation of the reference, not of the claim: PBH (tolerance 1e-7 on singular values) accepted one model whose theta* keeps a double root at -1 (AC3.RN9, oracle and cancellation reject it), because repeated unit-circle eigenvalues are defective and the rank tests fail numerically; the author's generator never produces such a case (0 of 2000 differ in RN49/RN50/RN53), but PBH should not be treated as ground truth for repeated unit roots. Formal side (AS1): theta and phi of the whole model share no root inside the circle, so the cyclotomic-only cancellation is complete.

Reran the implementation test with another seed: seed 12 n=200 --impl in the project venv (AC3.RN2): R adam_bounds_checker() and Python adam_bounds_checker() both 0 differing decisions against the prototype in 200 ETS+ARIMA and 200 ETS+SARIMA models; max abs difference between penalty/1e100 and the prototype modulus 9.35e-7 (ETS+ARIMA, 118 inadmissible) and 9.53e-7 (ETS+SARIMA, 167 inadmissible), R and Python equal to 8 digits; author's RN53 0 differences and 9.5e-7; all within the 1.1e-6 threshold (the C++ bisection returns the upper end, tolerance 1e-6). Script review: R positional call of adam_bounds_checker() matches its signature, Python dict arguments match, AR reflection computed as in C++; matrices are the author's builder verified against adam() on 30 models (AC3.RN1, gap 4.9e-15) not matrices from adam() fits. Limitations to state with the claim: (1) the prototype decides with a 1e-6 margin (modulus < 1 - 1e-6) and the package with modulus > 1 + 1e-50, so for a root exactly on the unit circle that does not cancel the package's answer is set by roundoff: simple cases (MA(1) theta=+-1, 1 - B + B^2, 1 + B^2) are rejected with modulus 1.00000095 (AC3.RN13), but in 3 of 1750 models of the wider generator the package accepted a model whose theta* keeps a cyclotomic factor, with modulus 0.9999999999999969 and 0.99999999999971 (AC3.RN4, RN9, RN10; seed 33 and 34 specs printed in their stdout), while the cancelled-polynomial prototype and the exact oracle reject them. The generator of RN53 has no such models (the only unit-circle MA roots are over-differenced and cancel), so the confirmed statement holds for what it says, random ETS+ARIMA models away from the boundary. (2) RN53 ran at commit 7cf64144, before the shortcut of DC6 (b4a10cc6), and always with ets_model=True, so the pure-ARIMA shortcut branch is not covered by it (see my check of DC6). The compiled _eigenCalc in the venv (built 16:49) is newer than the header's last change (16:48), so RN53 and my AC3.RN2 ran the current C++.

Proved and tested. phi of the whole model is the product of the ETS part's (F block-diagonal): level and seasonals give Phi_n, n dividing the lag (roots on the unit circle), a damped trend adds 1/phi_damp (outside the circle for phi_damp < 1), the constant adds 1-B; ADAM's ARI polynomial is the ari polynomial (differences are cyclotomic, stationary AR roots strictly outside; AC3.RN3, AC3.RN11 verify phi = ari on adam() matrices to 1e-14). So phi has no root inside the circle and no non-cyclotomic root on it, hence shares no root with theta there; only cyclotomic factors can cancel on the circle. Independent argument for the equivalence with PBH: uncontrollable and unobservable modes of D have the eigenvalues of F (feedback and output injection leave them unchanged), which are all of modulus at most 1, so every eigenvalue of D above 1 is reachable and observable; at modulus 1 it is the cyclotomic cancellation that decides. Numerically, an exact oracle (Fraction determinants, exact gcd(theta, phi), which cancels any shared factor, not only cyclotomic) agrees with the cyclotomic-only cancellation on 1750 wider-generator models (AC3.RN4-RN10, 0 differences). Unstated preconditions to add: damped phi at most 1 (adam bounds it to [0,1]; phi above 1 puts a root of phi inside the circle) and the AR actually being checked for stationarity (not the case when the AR parameters are provided and not estimated, where the premise fails); for adaptive regressors (time-varying w) the assumption is not covered.

The shortcut is exact. Derivation: a constant or static regressor has F row e_x, g_x = 0, so row x of D is also e_x and expanding det(I - D L) along it gives theta_whole = theta_ARIMA (1 - B) and phi_whole = phi_ARIMA (1 - B) (checked on adam() matrices of plain, constant and static-regressor ARIMA, 295 models in total, max gap 1.4e-14, AC3.RN3, AC3.RN11). With every MA factor invertible theta_ARIMA has no root on or inside the circle, the (1 - B) factors cancel with phi, so theta* has all roots outside; this holds whether or not the AR is stationary. Code: in R (adam_bounds_checker in R/utils-adam.R and ssarima in R/adam-ssarima.R) and Python (cost_functions.py) the whole check is skipped only when no ETS, no adaptive regressors, arima_model true and ma_reflection < 1, otherwise it runs, so an MA root that cancels with a difference is still accepted (reflection >= 1 goes to the whole check). maReflection is the factor-by-factor Schur-Cohn value, below 1 exactly when every factor is invertible. Tests (mine, the author has no recorded run of the shortcut: RN53 only used ets_model=True and predates b4a10cc6; RN55/RN56 are timing): on 238 adam()-built pure ARIMA models (plain 80, constant 80, static regressor 78; AC3.RN11) 136 have all MA roots outside the circle and smooth_eigens rejects 0 of them; the real R adam_bounds_checker() with etsModel FALSE (AC3.RN12) gives a penalty on 0 of the 136 and its decision equals the forced whole-model check on all 102 non-invertible ones (20 of them are accepted, the cancelling roots). RN55 and RN56 give identical log-likelihoods for the SARIMA (-541.382357389734 both) as the author's NT24 says. Minor: in floating point the shortcut is if anything more robust than the whole check (no cancellation tolerance involved); DC6's text 'the whole model is checked only otherwise' is right but reads as if non-invertible models were rejected, which they are not.
